what: The painterly shader (web/shaders/paint: prep to a display colour and its Kubelka-Munk pigment latent, the smoothed structure tensor, the anisotropic Kuwahara filter on pigment latents, flow-following brush relief and stroke identity, relief with XDoG lines and lit impasto, compose with temperature push, broken colour, value massing and the watercolour glaze) and its advected canvas for a moving camera (decide, advect and distortion), in the C++ core (ADR 0019). Same links as the earlier bounds files: JavaScript reference against the C++ reference (CPU link), and the C++ reference against the one WGSL source on D3D12 (WARP), WebGPU (SwiftShader) and Vulkan (lavapipe). Written before the C++ reference, the WGSL rewrite and the first run.
author_decisions: 2026-10-15: "No, renderer first"; "One C++ core". Coordinator, 2026-10-17: paint first, the author wants one unified painted look across Low Water.
controls: Every link carries a built-in control that must fail on every case of every run; a run whose control passes fails as a whole. Separately, one constant in the C++ reference and one in style.wgsl are edited by hand, rebuilt and run, the result recorded in evidence/cpp-port-style-runs-11.json with the prediction below, and the edit reverted.
fixtures: The three case sets the web parity page runs (web/test/shaders-paint.html): the six still cases of evidence/shaders-paint-parity-bounds.json on streetScene(240, 150, 0) (dusk, or daylight for watercolour-day), offset canvas; the three advected-canvas sequences of evidence/shaders-paint-motion-parity-bounds.json on streetScene(160, 100, 0, camera) with motionVectors() between frames, compared on the last frame; and the six cases of evidence/shaders-paint-postframes-parity-bounds.json on the committed 960 x 600 post frames. Exported per case: the scene (and per motion frame the scene, motion vectors and distances), the JavaScript image (Float32Array) and its encodePaint8 codes, and the tensor weights.
reference_arithmetic: The JavaScript stores every pass's output (prep, tensor, blurs, Kuwahara, stroke, relief, image, canvas coordinates) as f32 and computes in float64 between; the C++ keeps those f32 stores.

cpu_link.codes: at most 1e-4 of channel values differ, none by more than 1 code, on every case of every set
cpu_link.canvas: motion sets: the layer state (ages, seeds, mean distortions) equal after the last frame
cpu_link.why: exp, log, pow, tanh, sinh and cosh may differ in the last bit between V8 and the C++ library; a stroke follows the flow for up to 16 steps, and its sign and fade decisions are made continuous by design, so such a difference stays near one f32 rounding.

gpu_link.why: The web bounds of each set: an f32 rounding can send one stroke down a different path; advected canvas coordinates drift by a fraction of a pixel between f32 and f64.

controls_detail.built_in: The C++ reference with the exposure multiplied by 1.1: it must exceed the CPU link bounds and the set's GPU bounds, on every case.
controls_detail.source_edit: C++: the XDoG difference weight 0.985 to 0.99. Prediction: the CPU link fails on every case (every preset draws lines). WGSL: the oil canvas weave period 3.2 to 3.0 in the canvas height. Prediction: WARP fails on the still cases with impasto (oil-grotesque, oil, gouache, grotesque-panned) and passes the two watercolour cases, whose compose does not read the relief's shading.
